**What type of PR is this?**
/kind flake


**What this PR does / why we need it**:
As error log show in https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/directory/pull-kubernetes-bazel-test/1303342948955459585:
```
    csi_test.go:558: csiTest.VolumeAll preparing detacher.Detach...
E0908 15:00:03.081837      23 csi_attacher.go:632] kubernetes.io/csi: VolumeAttachment [vol2] has been deleted, will not continue to wait for attachment
    csi_test.go:310: csiTest.VolumeAll attacher.Attach failed: volume attachment has been deleted
    csi_test.go:568: csiTest.VolumeAll detacher.Detach succeeded for volume simple-driver^vol2
```

It comes from the goroutine in `csi_test.go`https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/88e3c95d7c46431e0842e0fdc2cb99279c038515/pkg/volume/csi/csi_test.go#L307-L316 
Which will call `waitForVolumeAttachment` in `Attach` function:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/88e3c95d7c46431e0842e0fdc2cb99279c038515/pkg/volume/csi/csi_attacher.go#L124-L125

It obvious that `Detach` happens before  in this case: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bd39d3933be27d70bf27067fc494194be21f8ff4/pkg/volume/csi/csi_test.go#L565

So the reason for flaky is:
If `Attach` goroutine runs slow and before it runs to `waitForVolumeAttachment`, `Detach` has already done, then `Attach` function will reture error.

So my change here is to wait `Attach` is done before `Detach`.

By the way, before `Attach` will not report error in its wait logic until this [PR](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/63303).

review_comments: Do we want to close before checking error?
yes, we don't want to hang the test in case of an error

Ah yes my confusion was around thinking this was in the main thread of execution here, which would mean that if the encapsulating function returned first that the routine would be terminated. Not sure what the odds of that even happening would be, but this goroutine is not encapsulated by the main thread of execution. However, let's say the last test case was being run and we hit an error here, could we feasibly exit the encapsulating function _and_ the main thread of execution prior to calling `t.Errorf`, thus causing the test to pass (assuming no other errors)?
